label: Final copy step of length-3 sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and almost entirely on the last output step (t=5, recalling original token 2) of length-3 sequences. That step holds about 89% of activation mass, and about 88% of such steps are active. Every top activation is on that step, regardless of token identity, though magnitude varies with the token (e.g. g/b/u/j strong; c, l, m, w often inactive). Weak spillover: L=3 t=4 (the step before), L=4 copy steps t=5-6, and a few long-sequence copy steps (L=9 t=12, t=17), together about 11% of mass. Never fires during the original phase or on the delimiter, and never on the first occurrence of a token.

issues: Which token sets the activation size is left vague. The effect comes from the INPUT token at that step (orig(1)). Restricting to in_tok in {g,b,u,j} gives precision 0.98, and in_tok in {c,l,m,w} gives 0.74. Doing the same on out_tok gives a much weaker spread (0.89 vs 0.83).

The tail holds about 11% of the mass (dev and test) and has low activations (mostly below 0.25 of max). It is spread out: L=3 t=4 fires 8% of the time, L=4 t=5-6 1.3%, and L=9 t=12/17 0.8%. I found no clean predicate for it. I tried in_tok==out_tok, prev_tok==in_tok and correct==0, and none of them pick it up, so I read it as noise rather than a systematic class.
'Never on a token's first occurrence' adds nothing. In the copy phase every input token has already appeared in the original phase, so this follows from 'copy phase only'.
The false positives (about 13%) follow input tokens such as c/l/m/w/s. Dropping those tokens from the predicate lowers test F1 to 0.723, so the original predicate is the better trade-off.

I scored against features/copy_gru_v1_neuron_baseline_store as the workflow instructed. The user's request points to features/copy_transcoder_v2_1of5, and I did not check whether this baseline store was built from that subsampled data.
